title: Family History; Early Life
description: Constance Baker provides biographical details for herself and her family, noting her birth in Nampa, Idaho, and her family's history of ranching in Ola. She mentions her parents' backgrounds and her own education and career leading up to her divorce.

title: Work at Community Center; Outdoor Lifestyle
description: Constance describes her role as director for the Retired Senior Volunteer Program and her shift from drafting to working with people. She also discusses the versatility required in rural life and her preference for self-sufficiency.

title: Childhood Memories; Marriage and Divorce
description: She reminisces about her childhood on the ranch, including riding horses and swimming. She then discusses her quick courtship with Gary Baker, the emotional struggles of their fifteen-year marriage, and the process of rebuilding her life after their divorce.

title: Childbirth and Parenting; Social Life
description: Constance talks about childbirth experiences, her parenting philosophy of open communication, and her friendships. She reflects on how she developed her independence and found support from other women after her divorce.

title: Recreation; Advice for Rural Life; Current Activities
description: Baker discusses her hobbies, the challenges of socializing in small towns, and her current life in Lewiston. She shares advice on fitting into tight-knit communities and describes her current work schedule and leisure activities.

title: Grandmother's influence; family ties; ranch upbringing; salt lick boxes
description: Constance Baker talks about the influence of her close-knit ranch family, particularly her grandmother, who taught her to recognize spring plants, make daisy chains and dandelion weavings, and do drawn handwork. She recalls growing up in the small house near her grandmother's big house on the ranch and says she still feels a strong bond with the land, following the weather and welcoming rain. She also tells about buying ceramic sinks at a sale in Asotin to use as salt lick boxes for her father's cattle.
